q-162574.name: Question 1
q-162574.problem: Consider the positively (outward) oriented surface $S$ given by ${x}^{2}+(y-2)^{2}+{z}^{2}=9$ and the vector field $F=(yz-2x)\,i+3y\,j+(x+z)\,k.$ Use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
q-162574.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(yz-2x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+z) \\  & =-2+3+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $3$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2\,\text{d}V \\  & =2{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =2\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {3}^{3} \\  & =72\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

q-162576.name: Question 2
q-162576.problem: Consider the positively (outward) oriented surface $S$ given by $(x-1)^{2}+{y}^{2}+(z+3)^{2}=16$ and the vector field $F=(x+2y)\,i+(4z-y)\,j+(z+xy)\,k.$ Use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
q-162576.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+2y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(4z-y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z+xy) \\  & =1+(-1)+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $4$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}1\,\text{d}V \\  & =1{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & ={∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =\text{Volume}(R) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {4}^{3} \\  & =\frac{256\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-162580.name: Question 3
q-162580.problem: Consider the positively (outward) oriented surface $S$ given by $(x+2)^{2}+(y-1)^{2}+{z}^{2}=1$ and the vector field $F=({y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\,i+4y\,j+2xz\,k.$ Use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
q-162580.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.

$$

$$

$$

q-162596.name: Question 4
q-162596.problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1,$ $x=e,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=0,$ $z=2.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=y\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,i+{z}^{2}\,j+(x-{y}^{3})\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
q-162596.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x-{y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{y}{x}+0+0 \\  & =\frac{y}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}z \\  & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{x=1}^{x=e}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\cdot [z]_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡e-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot (\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2})\cdot (2-0) \\  & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot (2-0) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

q-162597.name: Question 5
q-162597.problem: Let $S$ be the boundary of the rectangular prism enclosed by the planes $x=1,$ $x=3,$ $y=0,$ $y=2,$ $z=-1,$ $z=1.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=(y-{x}^{2})\,i+xy\,j+3xz\,k,$ find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
q-162597.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-{x}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(3xz) \\  & =(-2x)+x+3x \\  & =2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid region enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2x\,\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}2x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z \\  & =[{x}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=3}\cdot (2-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =(9-1)\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$
